_about: Inventory of code in this PUBLIC repo that can write to a public GitHub repo. This is a tripwire, not a proof. tests/public-writer-inventory.test.mjs scans workflows, composite actions and scripts for known ways of writing to GitHub (git push, gh pr, issue, release and api writes, curl and wget writes to the GitHub API, an HTTP write verb in a file that talks to GitHub, octokit and PyGithub write methods, GraphQL mutations, the repo's own write helpers, local writes to the public record files, write scoped workflow tokens and known write actions) and fails if a match neither calls setup/public-write-gate.mjs nor is listed below with a reason. A listed file is pinned to the rule ids that were reviewed, so new write code added to it fails CI. It cannot see writes built at run time, new callers of an already listed helper, languages it does not scan, writes made from another repo, by a person or through the gateway GitHub tools, or what a workflow prints to its public logs; those need a human reviewer. Anything that records findings, notes or diagnostics must use the gate. Finance, legal, investor, deal, inside information, privileged, PHI and personal findings never go to a public repo; record them in the private ledger (memory_remember with type finding, or task_create). A new exemption needs a reason of at least 20 characters, the rule ids it covers, and a reviewer who agrees the code writes no findings or lane-tagged records.

The pager issue helper. It opens or comments on one alert issue per alerting workflow with check names, statuses, run links and secret redacted log tails produced by the repo's own monitors. No agent authored findings and no lane. Exempt rather than gated on purpose: a gate that refused an alert would silence a pager, the failure class this helper exists to prevent. Follow up: a gate that degrades to fixed text instead of refusing.
